column1: # INTRA-BAR RANGE + VOLUME: the anchor vector for the bar channels (`rangeScale`, `volIdio`),
# which BarsAnchorSuite / bars_anchor_tests re-derive from this file. Editing a graded row moves
# the shipped test bands; editing a `const` row must be accompanied by the code constant it pins.
# Measured 2026-09-01 and re-read 2026-10-04 from Yahoo Finance's daily history (OHLC
# split- but not dividend-adjusted, and volume), read through 2026-08-31: SPY from 1993-01-29 =
# w1993, QQQ from 1999-03-10 = w1999.  The rows that read only prices reproduce the first read to
# within one unit of their last digit; the volume rows are this fetch's, up to 0.008 from it.
#   range x = ln(H/L) per session; with `-overnight` off the model's bar has NO overnight (open
#     = prior close) and the record's overnight variance share (row overnightShare) is the
#     commensurability haircut; with it on that row is GRADED (tol 0.10, since 0.23.1). Rows suffixed `Intraday` are measured against |ln(C/O)| / sign(C-O) — the fair
#     ruler for a no-overnight model; Parkinson recovers real INTRADAY vol (1.01 SPY, 1.00 QQQ),
#     which is what validates the pair of rulers.
#   r = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}); sd and var are population moments.  overnightShare = var(ln(O_t/C_{t-1}))
#     / var(r), the model's open reading; parkinson = sqrt(mean x^2 / 4 ln 2) / sd(r); downup rows
#     split sessions on the sign of r (Intraday: of C-O), ratios of mean range and differences of
#     mean volume; the trailing 21-session vol (rows *CorrVol21) includes the session.
#   volume v = ln(volume) minus its rolling 252-session median (the secular share-count trend
#     is not the statistic); rx = ln(x) minus its rolling 252-session median.  Both medians are
#     trailing and include the session; the volume rows start once they have 252 sessions.
#   const rows: the volume channel's frozen structural constants, from the DISTRIBUTED-LAG
#     regression v_t ~ rx_t + rx_{t-1} (0.519/0.143 SPY, 0.502/0.151 QQQ; lag 2 adds 0.04 and
#     is dropped -- a single-lag fit reads 0.58-0.60 because it absorbs the lag through the
#     range's own autocorrelation) and the SINGLE-lag fit's residual, which the resid* and
#     crossRxResid1 rows read (sd 0.29-0.38, acf1 0.51-0.57, acf5/acf1 = 0.82-0.84 => a slow
#     AR-0.97 component at ~0.55 of residual variance + white noise; residual down-up +0.037 =>
#     volDown 0.046 via E[max(-z,0)] = 0.8 on down days, frozen at 0.045). The lag term is what
#     carries the record's CROSS-persistence: corr(rx_t, resid_{t+1}) rows below.  The constants
#     stay frozen: none moves by more than 0.001 on the public re-read, a tenth of its
# The `tol` column is the twins' test band half-width (median of 4 model paths, 100y, at
# -rangescale 0.63 -volidio 0.34). Rows with `-` are documentation and grading-time anchors,
# read on -barsemit output by the conventions above; the model's
# disclosed residuals against them: corrRangeAbsR 0.82 vs the intraday 0.79-0.80 and volAcf1
# 0.59 vs 0.64-0.70 (one root: the bridge draws' lag-0 noise). The sign<->vol root is CLOSED by
# `rangeDown` 0.09: range downup 1.137 vs the intraday 1.109-1.142 and volume down-up 0.097 vs
# the intraday-sign gap 0.094-0.098 (rows volDownupGapIntraday) — the raw cc-sign gaps 0.123/
# 0.133 carry the overnight conditioning the model does not have.
